### COMMENTARY

...that the spirit of Nitre and Sulfur might invade metals and be able to reduce them into vitriol <note>In this context, vitriol refers to metallic sulfates, which were often seen as "seeds" or intermediate stages of metallic transformation.</note>; this, by Hercules, is truly to be admired in the highest degree and is most worthy of deep contemplation. However, it is not my intent here that you merely learn to use the distinction between fire, Sulfur, Mercury, and air, as well as similarly between false nitre, the spirit of tartar, and its clarified and fortified salt.

9. For although *Tartar* <note>A potassium salt (potassium bitartrate) that crusts in wine casks; highly valued by alchemists as a purifying agent.</note> is indeed from the Vegetable Kingdom, the Archaeus of nature <note>A Paracelsian term referring to the "internal chemist" or the vital force that directs the growth and transformation of matter.</note> has joined this vegetable to minerals with a certain singular kinship, and communicated a wondrous property to it. This is to such an extent that this vegetable yields nothing to nitre—except that, just as nitre, by reason of the circle and heat, is to be compared and dedicated to the Sun, so Tartar, by reason of the square and the cube, is to be compared to the earth. For it possesses, besides these, a certain dry and earthy property, and it is called the "field vegetable" <note>original: *vegetabile arvens*</note>. It has a singular sympathy with the Salt of metals, just as those salts relate magnetically to one another, because the seed of metals is sustained in this vegetable earth and is defended against its enemies. The enemy of all seeds is the combustive fire, and the adversary of tartar is common Sal Ammoniac <note>Ammonium chloride; often used to "open" metals or as a flux in alchemical operations.</note>.

10. Tartar improves metals and renders them malleable, so that it accords with the Metallic Salt, which is multiplied by tartar: for the abundance of the salt of metals is malleability, and if a metal is now made more malleable through tartar, then indeed it must be true that its Salt has been augmented. By the aid of tartar, metals pass into living Mercury <note>Quicksilver.</note>; this occurs because, while the Salt increases in quantity, the earth begins to dominate and bursts the bonds. For when the earth increases, the spirit—*which is an intense spirit, not an extended one*—is forced to dilate itself excessively, and thus causes a separation, and visibly contracts itself into living Mercury, since the earth has triumphed and has snatched away the governance from that through which the soul had previously directed the earthy body.

The "first metal" is that in which the metallic nature begins, and it is called the first matter <note>original: *materia prima*; the primal, undifferentiated substance that exists before it takes on a specific form.</note>. Where nature now stops and rests, there Art <note>The "Art" refers to the work of the alchemist.</note> first begins, and makes nature its handmaid. Nature can raise no metal higher or further by itself, because gold—out of its three principles—has passed into a pure, constant coagulation and fixation <note>original: *coagulationem & fixationem*; terms referring to a substance becoming solid and resistant to the transformative power of fire.</note>. For this reason, it is difficult to destroy.

### Chapter five.

#### *On the nature and property of the first principle, Mercury.*

1. The common Mercury of the metals is of a warm temperament; its own quality is moisture and heat, hence it possesses a concordance with air. The philosophers <note>The "philosophers" here are the alchemical authorities of the past.</note> understand Mercury himself under the element of air because of the great affinity he holds with it. He is by nature fugitive <note>volatile or easily evaporated by heat</note>, spiritual, and bodily, like saltpeter, to which he is especially devoted above others, like fire or spirit. Mercury has much Sulfur and no Salt; he is specifically assigned to the lungs because of the element of air, which the lungs cannot do without. Mercury, like a spirit, pervades and penetrates the other two principles—namely, *Salt* and *Sulfur*, that is, *body* and *soul*—both of which he joins together through natural heat and constantly overcomes.

2. The philosophers call Mercury the medium for joining the soul with the body; for he carries the soul in his belly and dissolves the body so that the soul may dwell and delight within it. Besides this penetrability and other properties, he is of a dissolving nature due to his radical moisture <note>original: *humiditatem radicalem*; the fundamental life-fluid of a substance</note>, and is uniquely to be used in illnesses that take their origin from viscous tartar <note>original: *tartaro*; a term for stony or hardened deposits in the body, like kidney stones or gout</note>. And although Mercury indeed seems to have no agreement with tartar, this connection nevertheless intervenes because of his innate and hidden fire, and namely—

### Chapter six.

## *On the nature of the second principle, Sulfur, in general.*

And just as material fire is strengthened, sustained, and made powerful by the application of wood, it happens in no different a way with our intrinsic fire.

### Chapter seven.

->*On the property of the third principle, namely Salt.*<-

1. Salt is the preservation, stability, and hardening <note>original: *induratio*</note> of all things; it alone preserves them from decay. Therefore, nature has added it as a companion and protector to all fixed elemental things or stable creations. It is the most constant of the fiery principles, which must preserve the other two <note>Sulfur and Mercury</note> in their being and state; and it is of an earthy nature.

2. The "Earth of the Wise" <term>Terra Sapientum: an alchemical term for the stable, material base of the Great Work</term> is Salt, which alone is indestructible, incombustible, and unconquerable. Because of its overpowering and excellent virtues, the ancient philosophers compared Salt to the divine majesty, and ascribed a certain divine power to it, even calling it *Electrum* <note>In this context, it refers to a "shining" or superior substance rather than the gold-silver alloy.</note>. Unless God, the Ruler of Nature <note>original: *Physiarcha*</note>, had ordained this principle as a safeguard for both of the weaker principles—Sulfur and Mercury—His creation would have perished and been reduced to nothing. This is the fundamental truth: unless Almighty God had created Salt, the Philosopher’s Stone could never be made; for Salt alone performs the preservation and fixing <note>original: *fixio*; the process of making a substance stable so that it no longer evaporates or changes in fire</note> of every thing. It is most notably found in the blood and the bladder of humans.

3. The salt of all metals provides their malleability <note>the ability to be hammered or pressed into shape without breaking</note>, and it is through a lack of salt that they are brittle. Saturn <term>Saturn: the alchemical name for the metal Lead</term> proves this, for it is made largely of salt, as its calcination <note>the process of heating a metal until it turns into a fine powder or ash</note> testifies. The salt of metals is a truly sublime medicine: whatever Mercury and Sulfur provide in medicine, Salt sets out to improve and strives to surpass. This occurs because it liquefies more easily and spreads itself out, and in this way preserves the human sulfur and the vital spirit, defending it against all diseases.

## Chapter Eight.

### *Whether the Universal Medicine is to be found in the seven stars—that is, in the seven metals—or rather, whether it is to be found in gold and the primary matter?*

<margin>1.</margin>
All philosophers who before this time and up to this day have written about the *Universal Medicine and the primary matter* <term>materia prima: the formless primeval substance from which all things are created</term>, are not only of differing and conflicting opinions, but are also so obscure that in their discourse no foundation is to be found. For sometimes they seem to mean common *Mercury and Saturn* <note>In alchemical texts, Saturn often refers to lead.</note>, and then again they seem to signify *nitre* <note>Saltpeter</note>, or *vitriol* <term>vitriol: a sulfate mineral, often iron or copper sulfate, used for its corrosive properties</term> alone. They also use these or those names for themselves, when nevertheless they mean something quite different. There were very few philosophers who did not always indicate and describe the matter metaphorically or otherwise by some involved path. Indeed, they treat more fully of the medicinal virtue, power, and efficacy than they do of the thing itself, so that it is no wonder [one cannot] properly distinguish it or [know] where we might find it. They do not explain how, once the knowledge of the matter is obtained (without which nothing can be accomplished), we ought to proceed most briefly and certainly; hence it is said that, by concealing the matter, they have only revealed the effect. I, however, am going to give an open and certain demonstration here, such as has never been made before me. For I shall deal here most clearly, not concerning the virtues, but more truly concerning the matter itself, and how it is to be drawn toward medicine, using common words and a simple style. I do this for the reason that nearly all philosophical books abound with the proclamations of titles [concerning virtues], yet there has been doubt concerning the matter itself until now.

<margin>2.</margin>
Therefore, I commend to you again, under the seal of your conscience, that our matter is to be compared to the whole world and the entire orb of the earth, certainly as far as its virtues are concerned. For it is the attractive force of all mineral and metallic things, because the *Soul* <note>original: *Anima*</note> or *Spirit* <note>original: *Spiritus*</note>

<summary>In this chapter, the author criticizes previous alchemists for their intentional obscurity regarding the "primary matter" of the Universal Medicine and promises a clear, plain-language explanation of what this substance actually is. He asserts that this matter holds an attractive power over all minerals and metals, containing their soul and spirit.</summary>

## Chapter Ten.

### On the nature and property of the terrestrial planet Jupiter
->tin.<-

That ash-colored <note>original: "Cineritius"</note>, honest, and just Jupiter has his influence on the terrestrial Jupiter <note>The metal tin</note>, which, after its preparation, shows itself with a clear, airy, and sweet salt and lunar sulfur, and presents its virtues to mortals. That good Jupiter also has his special influence on the liver; it therefore heals the liver and all ailments that arise from it. Because of this, I do not wish to occupy myself any longer with Jupiter, but I proceed to that most powerful leader of war, whom the philosophers title the Iron Captain <note>A reference to the planet/god Mars, the symbol for Iron</note>.

### Chapter eleven.

## *On the nature and property of Mars, iron.*

The philosophers say, *He who is ignorant of Mars does not know the Art* <note>original: "Qui ignorat Martem, non novit Artem"</note>; that is, he who does not know nor recognize the qualities of iron is not a true craftsman. He who does not know how Mars is to be destroyed—through that which lies hidden within himself—and likewise reduced back into his first matter, that same man, for all his chemical strategies, is of little use to the invincible martial leader of war in his time of greatest need.

2. Mars possesses a solar, hot sulfur; from the outside he indeed appears *white*, but from within he is *red*. His Salt is so matured and animated by his own sulfur that he gives much trouble even to the "fugitive robber"—namely, <term>Mercury: quicksilver, known in alchemy for its volatility and refusal to be "fixed" or solidified</term>. For the salt of Mars can constantly coagulate and fix Mercury, especially when old Saturn <note>The metal lead</note> comes to his aid with his double sword and armor. Without Saturn's help and support, however, Mars will be able to achieve nothing difficult or heroic against his enemies, nor in favor of his friends. This is because coagulation (as all philosophers testify along with me) is found only in Saturn. I have indicated somewhat above the path by which defiant Mars may reach an equilibrium and a treaty with this Saturn, rendering himself a sharer in Saturn’s aid; for he must first be reduced to his three principles <note>The alchemical "tria prima": Salt, Sulfur, and Mercury</note>, and this by means of *Magical* fires, which are the philosophical elements and the keys of health. Therefore, see that you grasp my meaning correctly; reread my writings often, until you have firmly fixed a fundamental understanding in your mind. This, however, cannot and will not happen if you imagine that I am adopting a bombastic philosophical style <note>original: "cothurnico-philosophicum," referring to the "cothurnus" or high-soled buskin worn by tragic actors, implying a grand, tragic, or overly-ornate way of speaking</note>. As I have described and depicted these things to you, so they shall always stand before your eyes—in no other form, appearance, or figure—just like a beautiful little painting.

In the same way, the noble Mars once experienced enough of this with **Venus** <note>In alchemy, Venus represents Copper</note> and her spirit—not without mockery and the shame of the other planets, as the poet tells the tale <note>A reference to the mythological story where Vulcan catches Mars and Venus in a net, exposing them to the ridicule of the gods</note>. <header>DISCOURSE</header>

Also, from the external gestures of Mars and his apparent posture, and from his father, mother, and all his ancestral relatives, it may be quite easily discerned what kind of man he becomes, since his person rules, restrains, and brings the whole world, as it were, under his feet. For Mars is a cross and a scourge to the world, by which its inhabitants are punished and driven toward the amendment of their sinful ways. Although I could still say enough here for the benefit and favor of miners and mineral consultants: for truly with great profit and in a very short time, we are able to elevate **iron** <note>original: "ferrum"</note> into excellent **steel** <note>original: "chalybem"</note> with significant gain; and similarly, over a longer period, we are able to elevate **Mars** <note>Iron</note> into **Venus** <note>In this context, the author refers to the alchemical transmutation of a "base" metal like iron into a more "refined" or "noble" state, often associated with copper or gold in these allegories</note>. 7. Now I prepare myself for medicine. Mars heals, first and foremost, all defects that arise and are derived from **bile** <term>bile: also called choler; in the medical theory of the time, an excess of this "hot and dry" fluid was thought to cause anger and fever</term>, through a certain unique and mystical sympathy; otherwise, his **sulfur** <note>In Paracelsian medicine, Sulfur represents the combustible, soul-like principle of a substance</note> is uniquely suited for the heart and liver. The **Salt of Mars** <term>Salt of Mars: A chemical preparation of iron (such as iron sulfate), used as a tonic to treat anemia and digestive issues</term> excels in the Chemical art; moreover, the same has retained a famous name for itself in medicine: for it is beneficial for all diseases that have proceeded from inflamed human sulfur. And since the gall, besides salt, carries with it a very virulent and watery sulfur, the Salt of Mars heals all stomach fevers which an excess of bile has caused, and many similar ailments. ### Chapter thirteen.

## *On the nature and property of Venus, copper.*

1. **Lascivious Venus** <note>original: *lasciva Venus*. In alchemy, Venus is the traditional name for the metal copper, often described as "lascivious" or "wanton" because of how easily it reacts and combines with other substances.</note> has an entirely earthly body, which is filled with a certain sublime solar sulfur. However, because of the weakness of its "bones" and its infirm, impure dwelling-place, this sulfur was not able to make a stable home for itself therein; for when it is necessary for the body to be destroyed, the soul departs and deserts its habitation. Whoever now knows how to nourish and preserve this soul through **Magic** elements in the fire, and afterwards how to extract it from the calcined <term>calcined: reduced to a powder or ash by the action of high heat.</term> body, has obtained the true meaning of this little book, for he will be able to rejoice in the light that shines for him. This sulfur, with which Venus is clothed, far surpasses the solar sulfur in its color, for the reason that the sulfur of the sun is notably improved by the sulfur of Venus. For just as the true **Sun** <note>original: ☉, the symbol for the Sun and Gold.</note> nourishes itself with the blood of the **green lion** <term>green lion: A famous alchemical symbol, usually referring to "vitriol" (sulfuric acid) or a specific mineral ore capable of dissolving gold.</term>, and thus is made entirely bloody and ignited; so in the same way, gold also delights in, feeds upon, and strengthens itself with the tincture of Venus and Mars <note>Mars is the alchemical name for Iron.</note>. Therefore, it was not in vain, nor without reason, that the philosophers said: *The Sun does not tinge, unless it is tinged.* <note>original: *Sol non tingit, nisi tingatur*. This refers to the idea that gold cannot transform other metals unless it is first "colored" or empowered by the essences of other metals.</note>

If our philosophical King (that is, gold) is to do good for his servants and courtiers, and make them wealthy and raise them to high ranks of honor, then it is necessary that he too first demand impositions, contributions, taxes, or simple collections from his subjects. For the most powerful leader in war, *Mars* <note>In alchemical symbolism, Mars represents the metal **iron**.</note>, knows a thousand ways and means—sometimes through taxes, sometimes through clearances, reparations, or through armaments, fortifications, and collections of every kind—to command that everything be spent in the service and interest of the kingdom, according to the instructions of his king and Sovereign. *Mars* can do this and even something greater: for he is the reason and the rule that where the subjects are wealthy, the kings must necessarily be poor; and wherever the kings are opulent, the subjects there are destitute and obedient, and consequently, no rebellion is to be feared. And if perhaps some sedition should arise out of desperation, *Mars is immediately present* and settles the matter; for this reason, *Mars* is held in the highest esteem at court, because he is the strength and honor of the kingdom.

3. *Venus* <note>In alchemical symbolism, Venus represents the metal **copper**.</note> indeed, although she can make the king prosper through cunning—just as her husband *Mars* does—she herself rests neither day nor night. Instead, she uses her own body and stands for sale to everyone for money, whether they be members of the clergy or the laity, single or married; this is nothing to her, since she prostitutes herself to everyone for the sake of wealth. For she must give her king a yearly tribute, both ordinary and extraordinary, so that the king may grow rich. In short, *Venus* performs her duties vigorously and is a faithful handmaid to the king, as can be seen in the primary cities of hot and luxurious regions, where the high court—to avoid "sodomitic" sins <note>A historical reference to the legal and religious practice of regulating prostitution to prevent what were then considered more "deviant" sexual acts.</note>—assigns *Venus* a permanent seat and palace, and grants this in exchange for a certain annual tribute. Just as it is now necessary for this *Venus* to contribute as a subject of the king, so similarly must our *Venus* <note>The alchemist is now speaking specifically of the "philosophical" or purified copper used in the lab.</note> contribute her body—and especially her soul, which is rich in gold—to provide splendor. And although *Venus* is sufficient in performing this, yet she is not alone; for everything besides *Venus* that is found with red metallic sulfur is related to the star of the **Sun** <note>original: *Solis*. In alchemy, the Sun always represents Gold.</note>, and it willingly allows itself to be fermented with the sulfur of the **Sun**, because like has its origin from its like; therefore, like always and continually rejoices in its like.

4. From there, with the help of **sal ammoniac** <note>Ammonium chloride, used as a flux and cleaning agent in alchemy.</note>, the true **Virgin’s Milk** <term>Virgin's Milk: Latin *lac virginis*, a name for various white chemical precipitates or a specific stage of the solvent.</term> comes forth. That permanent water is the blameless, genuine universal solvent; it is that true **Hermaphroditic spirit**, that twofold Mercury, the unique medium for dissolving and for joining the soul with the body, and so forth. And although the body of Venus is infected with a horrible **leprosy** <note>In alchemical texts, "leprosy" refers to the impurities or oxidation found in base metals like copper.</note>, she nevertheless produces magnificent effects and great wonders after her preparation.

Furthermore, the **Sulphur of Venus** <term>Sulphur: In alchemy, one of the three "Primes" representing the soul, combustible principle, or active force of a metal.</term> is also a medicine for the heart, just like the **Sulphur of Mars** <note>Sulphur derived from iron.</note>; this is because they are **solar** <note>original: *solaria*; meaning they share the life-giving, golden qualities of the Sun.</note>, as I have provided information above. She uniquely contributes to the *Great Work of the Sages* <term>Great Work: Latin *Magnum Opus*, the process of creating the Philosopher's Stone.</term>, especially her soul, which reveals itself in the form of a reddish, heavy oil. By the Sulphur of Venus, the internal sulphur of man is improved, strengthened, and restored entirely; for it also dries up **dropsy** <note>An old medical term for edema or swelling caused by excess fluid.</note>, serves the liver, and settles all fluxes of the blood in both men and women—especially, indeed, when some of the universal solvent has adhered to it, which is difficult to separate from the soul without its presence. And just as it is difficult to segregate the spirit from its own soul, so also it is not possible to separate our solvent from its solute without damage.

### Concerning the nature and properties of the fugitive Mercury.

1. The ancient philosophers placed Mercury only at the second table of honor, which is greatly to be wondered at, since Mercury is by nature noble and proud, and lifts himself above all the stars to denote that his seat ought by right to be higher, and that the supreme honor is owed to him; since within him the highest secret of human health <note>original: *sanitatis humanæ arcanum*</note> is to be found. He is, moreover, sociable toward all stars because of his astral seed; and the planet with which he joins is strengthened in its own position. Thus, if that planet be malicious, Mercury is rendered even more malicious; but if it be benign, then that planet is improved through the union with Mercury and strengthened in its purpose. In short, Mercury is like a neutral man or a politician <note>The author compares the chemical "indifference" of Mercury—its ability to alloy with many metals—to a diplomat who tries to please everyone.</note>, who willingly offends no one but pleases all. Furthermore, he is by nature hot and fiery in his whole being. The **metallic fire** <term>Metallic fire: The internal, essential heat believed to reside within metals, driving their growth and transformation.</term> is so effective in Mercury that his body must remain in a continuous state of flow.

2. And although this Mercury has many virtuous medicinal faculties and powers within himself, he is indeed still far from being the **Mercury of the Philosophers** <term>Mercury of the Philosophers: A sophisticated alchemical substance, distinct from common quicksilver, believed to be the "First Matter" of the Stone.</term>; for the Mercury of the Philosophers is the Mercury of metals, which is never [merely] hot and cold, or dry and hot, etc. because it encompasses within itself the qualities of the four elements <note>Earth, Air, Fire, and Water.</note>. Common Mercury, however, is hot in its whole being; therefore, it cannot be the Mercury of the Philosophers. And although this is so, nevertheless, one must not for that reason despise or reject it, since the ancient Sages always held him in high and sublime regard, having adorned him with the moon <note>Symbol for Silver.</note> and distinguished him with the sun <note>Symbol for Gold.</note> in place of a well-deserved crown.

Hence the inconsistent Mercury congratulates himself in every way on the humanity and loveliness of Venus, which those who are "sharp-nosed" <note>original: *nasuti*; an idiom for those who are discerning, clever, or have a "scent" for secrets.</note> will weigh with particular care. And since this pertains to the more secret seal of the Sages, I shall cease for now, leaving you meanwhile to examine the aforementioned Mercury with its Venusian properties. May the Gods favor the undertakings.

## Chapter Fifteen.
### *On the nature and property of the phlegmatic Moon.*

1. The Moon exerts its astral influence, by the help of cold Saturn, upon the ore of silver; this ore acts as a receptacle for lunar powers and further communicates its goodness to Mortals. And just as the Moon has its influence upon silver, specifically manifesting its operations within it, so too does it govern the brain in the microcosm <note>microcosm: literally "small world," referring to the human being as a reflection of the greater universe (the macrocosm).</note>. From this it follows that the "lower Moon"—namely, silver prepared for this specific purpose—heals all defects of the brain fundamentally. This is because this power was communicated to the silver by the "upper Moon" in the heavens; For that which is below is like that which is above, etc. <note>original: *Nam illud, quod est inferius, est sicut illud, quod est superius*; a famous axiom from the Emerald Tablet of Hermes Trismegistus, expressing the correspondence between the celestial and terrestrial realms.</note> When the upper Moon is hindered in its benign operations by other contrary planetary aspects—which stand in opposition to the Moon, wishing to bring about something other than what the Moon intends, or otherwise to "infect" it—then not only is the lower Moon (as the receptacle of that superior virtue) weakened in its spirit and obstructed in its operation, but the human brain also suffers as a result, according to the nature of that celestial infection. Thus, an "astral disease" arises, by which the microcosm is afflicted. Such infirmities can scarcely be cured in the common way through herbal remedies <note>original: *Vegetabilia*; plant-based medicines.</note>, since plants are situated in a lower and unequal degree of power compared to the stars. For these reasons, we must take in hand a medicine of a more sublime degree, or at least one that persists in the same degree as the affliction, as for example:

2. If the Moon is infected and suppressed by very wicked, poisonous, and opposing planets, the human brain (as its receptacle) is consequently weakened or infected. If this disease is to be cured, it must be done through sympathetic medicine <term>Sympathetic medicine: A system of healing based on the "law of signatures" or resonance, where substances with similar natures or celestial rulers are used to heal one another.</term>. This medicine, however, must itself first be freed and purged of every infection which it attracted to itself from its celestial superiors, so that it may persist alongside the primary cause in a proximate, equal, or even superior degree. Now, in truth, no one can deny that metals and gems [possess a] more noble...

### *On the nature and property of gems.*
### *How they are to be reduced to the sublime medicine through the Philosophers' Universal Solvent <note>original: Menstruum Universale; in alchemy, a "menstruum" is a solvent capable of dissolving solids or extracting their essence.</note>?*

1. **G**ems have their principle and origin from the astral "first mover" <note>original: *primo mobili*; in the old geocentric model of the universe, this was the outermost sphere that imparted motion to all others.</note>, just as the highest and lowest metals do. From this source, gems correspond—through their colors, sulfurs <note>In alchemy, "sulfur" represents the active, combustible, or "soul" principle of a substance, not just the chemical element.</note>, and other properties—to the stars above and below. They perform their operations only once they have been liberated from their earthly bonds and the "bundles of the earthly curse" <note>A common alchemical phrase referring to the impurities of raw matter that must be purged to reveal the divine essence within.</note>, and have been resolved into the Three Principles <note>Salt, Sulfur, and Mercury—the three building blocks of all matter in Paracelsian chemistry.</note>; this is achieved through the Universal Solvent. The same solvent that dissolves metals into sulfur and salt must also be employed for the extraction of the colors and salts of gems, since all things are brought down into a physical body by the single "spirit of the world" <note>original: *spiritus mundi*</note>. This spirit is the Universal Solvent itself, in which there is a certain attractive power for all things, whether mineral or metallic. It is called by Basilius <note>Referring to Basil Valentine, a famous, likely pseudonymous, 15th-century alchemist.</note> "All in All" <note>original: *Omnia in Omnibus*</note>. Believe me, the spirit of the Earth must lead its sulfur out of the earth and back into the earth again; therefore, in this spirit lies the supreme secret of the entire chemical science. Without this spirit, we would not have been able to perceive the goodness of the Creator hidden within gems.

2. And so that you do not pass by the medicine that can be found in gems, know that every gemstone has its own "star" <note>A specific celestial or planetary influence.</note> from which it receives its power and operation, just as metals do. Just as metallic medicines benefit the seven principal organs of humans, gems perform the same function. For instance: the Garnet, if it holds the influence of the Saturnine star and its ruler Orphiel <note>The planetary intelligence or angel traditionally associated with the planet Saturn.</note>, heals afflictions of the spleen. This is exactly like lead <note>The metal associated with Saturn.</note>, because both hold a single star that flows its nature from above to below. From this, it follows that minerals, vegetables, and even certain animals can possess the virtues of a single category.

**Topaz**, through the power of the Jovian influence <note>Jovian: pertaining to the planet Jupiter and the metal tin.</note> of **Zachariël**, aids the liver and all defects that arise from it. It does so in the same manner, and no less effectively, than "prepared Jupiter" <note>original: *præparatus Jupiter*; refers to alchemical preparations of the metal tin, which was traditionally used to treat the liver.</note> could or would be able to do. The sympathetic, Martial **Ruby** <note>Martial: pertaining to the planet Mars and the metal iron.</note> receives its power from the intelligence of **Mars**; since this is **Samuël**—a singular influence and virtue—it is therefore ordained for the bile and serves all defects that proceed from it.

3. The Solar **Carbuncle** <note>Carbuncle: a term used for deep red gems, such as high-quality garnets or rubies, believed to emit their own light.</note> surpasses the light, splendor, and virtue of all other gems because its governing intelligence is the most powerful **Michaël**, whose name means: *Who is like God?* <note>original: *Quis est ut Deus?*</note>

It is as if this intelligence wished to indicate that, just as nothing is higher than God, so nothing more sublime can be found in the world than God and the Solar Carbuncle. Nature wished to exalt the Carbuncle even above gold, because she has matured it fully—indeed, she has raised it even to the state of glass <note>original: *vitrum*; in alchemy, the "vitrification" of a substance was considered the ultimate state of perfection and fixity.</note>, which is the final and most perfect operation that nature or art is able to achieve. ## Chapter Seventeen.

### *Concerning the medicine of Plants and Animals, which manifests itself in those two kingdoms, and sympathetically relates to the primary medicine.*

1. We say, and it is true: *Man, wine, and gold are well-disposed toward one another.* Wine possesses an effective, strengthening Spirit, which is able to refresh the heart of man. Wine revives the spirit in the elderly, which otherwise lies buried so deeply within them, as if dead, that we cannot even perceive it. However, once wine is drunk by men and has formed a certain union with the animal and vegetable spirit, the **vital spirit**—namely, **Mercury** <note>In this context, Mercury refers to the "spirit" or life-force within the body, rather than the liquid metal.</note>—is excited by it. This spirit is spread through the entire body so that all the limbs perceive it and gain the power to move. Mercury rules the **microcosm** <note>The human being, viewed as a miniature reflection of the entire universe.</note>, and wine is the vehicle of both universal and particular medicine. What is more, the spirit of wine is not only a vegetable solvent, but also a mineral one. It possesses such a friendship with metals, just as a certain burning **sulfur** <note>original: "sulphur". In alchemy, sulfur represents the "soul" or the principle of combustion and color.</note> has with metallic sulfur; from this comes the fact that no Potable Gold can be made without it. The spirit of mercury extracts the **tincture** <note>The essential, healing essence of a substance.</note> from the sulfur of the sun <note>original: "sulphure solis". Alchemical shorthand for the soul of gold.</note> as the innermost part of the soul; the spirit of wine, however, extracts the innermost part of these innermost things, because there the dregs separate themselves again, which must not be introduced nor drawn into the tincture. The Tincture is a dry sulfur, which is dissolved by the **Mercury of the Philosophers**, and unites itself with it in such a way that the dissolved cannot be [separated] from the solvent.

...separate them, because they have merged like one water into another. This is because the gold cannot be separated from this first solvent at all, nor by any extraction, just as difficultly as water is separated from water, etc.

And this is a true sign, for the philosophers all agree on this point: that in the "Great Mastery" <note>original: "magisterio magno"; referring to the completion of the Great Work or the Philosopher's Stone.</note>, the solvent must certainly remain with the substance it has dissolved. This is indeed rightly and well pronounced, since the true solvent cannot be torn away from the solute, but must stay in digestion with it for at least twelve days and display a **red appearance**; only then should it be called true **Potable Gold**.

2. For it is very favorable to metals, increasing their malleability—that is, their **salt**—because salt is the malleability of metals. Therefore, whatever makes them malleable increases their salt. 

From this, we could also well—or rather, better—use the spirit of tartar to obtain the *three principles* <note>original: "tria principia"; the alchemical trio of Sulfur (soul/inflammability), Mercury (spirit/fluidity), and Salt (body/stability).</note>, as I indicated above. That is, a separation must follow in the *three principles* when the salt (or element of earth) is increased to such an extent that it begins to dominate; then the other two must immediately give way. However, since this is not the way nor the intention—that we should lose the **sulphur**—I leave this free to each individual, wishing at least to have warned them to consider it further. As for me, I am easily content with what I have experienced, until I find a better and closer

### *On the Chemical Alphabet.*

->How indeed the characters, signs, and words of the ancient philosophers<-
->are to be understood and interpreted.<-

1. In the preceding chapters, I have written clearly and explicitly enough regarding the First Matter <term>Materia prima: The formless, foundational substance from which all things are created, sought by alchemists as the starting point of the "Great Work."</term>, the Solvent <term>Menstruum: In alchemy, this is not a biological term but refers to a "philosophical solvent" capable of dissolving or extracting the essence from a substance.</term>, and the Universal Medicine; likewise regarding the Magical Elements or keys, as much as God has indeed permitted me. However, since this might happen to be somewhat difficult for beginning students—seeing as the philosophical style is still unknown to them, and I intend nothing else than to serve all faithful-hearted and honest Sons of the Art—I have found it highly necessary to take a starting point from a humble and simple understanding. I have decided to attach a Chemical Alphabet and certain new characters which truly exhibit the properties of the things they designate. Therefore, the fair lover of the arts will take unique care in examining this Alphabet and the attached new characters, for from there the first light arises.

2. The Philosophers have compared their matter, or solvent, to the sharpest vinegar, and likewise to vitriol or saltpeter, because this contains all the qualities which are attributed to the First Matter by the philosophers, since it is found to be wet and dry, cold and hot, light and heavy, according to how we wish to have it. Now, Mercury <note>In this context, "Mercury" refers to "Philosophical Mercury," the principle of fluidity and spirit, rather than just the common liquid metal.</note> likewise has this property, and it is clear that the Philosopher's Stone <term>Lapis Philosophorum: The legendary substance capable of turning base metals into gold and providing the Elixir of Life.</term> cannot be made without it; for that reason, the Wise do not act unjustly when they call their Matter "Mercury."

Indeed, for that reason, I have had to endure detraction <note>original: "detractionem"; criticism or belittling</note> from the virtuous as well as the wicked. To the wise and understanding, it is displeasing that I have written so clearly; the wicked, however—whom the Almighty does not favor—will think I have spoken too obscurely about the matter, or they will maintain other sinister opinions regarding it. Although the offense taken by those virtuous masters experienced in the art might rightly deter me, I nevertheless feel compassion, on the other hand, for the sincere and unlearned lovers of this art, with whom I wish to freely share my experience. I pity those who are exhausted and preoccupied by so many <term>ill-conceived books</term> <note>original: "cacochymicos libros"; literally "bad-juice" books, referring to works of pseudo-alchemy that lead to error or "bad chemistry"</note> and who labor in vain.

2. Therefore, know first that all things are formed and made from **three essences** <note>In alchemy, these are typically Salt, Sulfur, and Mercury</note> into this or a similar body, through **astral impression** and **elemental operation**. Elements are found in metals, and non-metals are found in the elements; for the "seed" of metals is not so far removed as certain self-styled scholars have imagined. And although the elements must cooperate in the formation of any body, they are not the <term>Prime Matter</term> <note>original: "materia prima"; the original "first stuff" of the universe</note> or that astral seed itself; rather, they are the cause of **generation and corruption**, and the corruption of one is the generation of another.

3. The ancient philosophers believe that every thing was created out of **hatred or love**, that is, out of **sympathy and antipathy**, as if from two mutually opposing qualities of the elements, which carry out this operation through celestial influence and special astral impression, etc. Now, the elements are incorporated within metals and minerals, and therefore they also possess those same qualities. There are only two pairs of opposing qualities through which whatever exists is generated and born: **Fire** is hot and dry, and its opposite is the cold, moist element of **Water**; **Air** is moist and hot, and its opposite is the dry, cold **Earth**. And since no body can be found outside of those four elements, and since the elements are incorporated in all things, a certain conflict arises from this in every element—

For these reasons, all things beneath the sphere of the moon are destined to perish and are destructible. Because while two contraries persist within a single subject, an unceasing struggle occurs, until at last one part receives aid from its external element; for then the opposing part must immediately withdraw and yield victory to the stronger. From this arises a certain corruption <note>In alchemy, "corruption" refers to the breakdown or decomposition of a substance so that a new form can emerge.</note>, or a separation of the entire substance, so that a new form lies before our eyes, which has been generated through that very corruption.

4. The elements of metals are their *three* primordial matrices <note>original: "matrices"; literally "wombs," referring to the formative origins or "Three Primes"</note>: Mercury, Sulfur, and Salt. These are like contraries in a state of continual battle and enmity. For Mercury, as an airy spirit, wages hostility against Salt, which represents earth; and hot Sulfur, like fire, is the enemy of water—namely, it is contrary to the moisture of Mercury. For in this context, Mercury is the water of metals and represents two elements: air and water. These aforementioned three matrices, or metallic elements, struggle for their nourishment from our material, visible, and tangible elements within their mortal home until a fixed time, until one element, through external support, becomes too strong for the other and suppresses it, since no help is provided to the weaker element by its own kind. 

And just as a human being falls into a serious illness when one element dominates within him—where first his fat (like sulfur) and afterwards even his flesh and blood fail, forcing him to die unless we provide the necessary restoration to the suffering or dominating element and establish a certain suitable harmony anew—for that reason, it is necessary for a physician to know which principle or element acts upon the patient and which one suffers. Just as it happens in the **microcosm** <note>The "little world," referring to the human body as a reflection of the universe.</note>, so it also occurs in metals and minerals; through the strengthening of one or another element, they suppress and suffocate the contrary element, from which corruption and separation must follow.

# PLAIN RECAPITULATION.

Saturn possesses two—or rather, only two—metals. Regarding those two mercuries, I have set forth with total truth, without guile or entanglement <note>original: "sine dolo & nodo"; a phrase meaning without hidden difficulties or deception</note>, that I would briefly instruct you on how you ought to behave in similar instances. Know, therefore, that when the Philosophers speak of their <term>Mercury</term> <note>the secret "First Matter" of the alchemists, not the common metal</note>, you must by no means understand it as the mercury of the common people <note>original: "mercurium vulgi"; common quicksilver</note>. Their mercury is metallic—the mercury of metals themselves. It is hot and dry, yet moist and cold. Common mercury, however, is hot in its entire essence; therefore, it cannot be considered or used as the Mercury of the Philosophers.

14. Common mercury carries the seed of silver within itself, but the other mercury obtained the <term>Sulfur of the Sun</term> <note>The active, "fiery" principle of gold</note> in metallic form and property from the Creator of heaven and earth. It is a **Solar Magnet**, just as common mercury may be called a **Lunar Magnet**. Mercury shows this to be so by its crescent moon symbol, with which the Sages have marked it to distinguish and separate it from the true Solar mercury. We distinguish these two mercuries by their smoke, which is their sulfur. One must also observe how volatile, fixed, or "fugitive" they are, and whether they allow themselves to be <term>sublimated</term> and <term>precipitated</term> <note>Sublimation involves heating a substance into vapor that then solidifies; precipitation is the process of a solid settling out of a liquid solution</note> quickly or slowly. This is the living way to tell these two mercuries apart.

15. And know further: just as Nature has generated two mercuries—the Lunar and the Solar—in the same way, through the Art <note>Alchemy</note>, a similar mercury can be prepared from those two fixed bodies. Indeed, what is more, a "living mercury" can also be made from the intermediate metals, such as **antimony**, **bismuth**, or **arsenic**, which are uniquely useful for medicine. Nevertheless, despite their excellent medicinal value, these are by no means to be judged or proclaimed as the Mercury of the Philosophers. This is because that true Mercury is the <term>Universal Menstruum</term> <note>original: "menstruum universale"; the ultimate solvent capable of dissolving all substances into their primal state</note>, and it is born twice from mercury: first from the Lunar, and then from the Solar. This mercury may rightly be named the ***double Mercury***.

It appears as an ore of mercury and is called the ***Lead of the Sages*** and the ***Azoth*** <note>The universal life force or essential "mercury" of the philosophers</note> of the philosophers, from which we are accustomed to distill the <term>Virgin’s Milk</term> <note>original: "lac virginis"; a white, mercurial liquid used in alchemical processes to dissolve or nourish the "Stone"</note>; it also possesses a <term>Venusian property</term> <note>Relating to copper or the power of growth and attraction</note>. 

The "last metal," however, is called the "last" because it has arrived at its mature perfection and its end. For the end <note>The ultimate goal or teleological purpose</note> of metals is to be **gold**; nature does not work further within metals beyond that point, but must desist and cease until Art—her mistress—comes to her aid. In a short span of time (though not without nature's help), Art proceeds so far that from the compact solar body <note>Gold</note>, a certain translucent, diaphanous little body arises, which the philosophers call ***vitrification*** <note>The process of turning a substance into a glass-like state; alchemists sought the "Glass of Gold" as a stage of extreme purification</note>. 

This is now the noblest thing that nature and art can achieve and work. However, I cannot properly describe here how this vitrification is to be performed or established; for a massive volume would arise from this compendium of mine, contrary to my intent. Nevertheless, lest I seem to wish to keep this for myself alone and carry it to the grave as so many of the ancient Sages have done, attend to this:

**19.** Take this *magical* fiery element, which is composed of two infernal, opposing materials, such as **sulfur and nitre** <note>original: "sulphure & nitro"; Saltpeter and sulfur, which together create a violent, explosive reaction</note>. With this infernal, consuming fire, begin where nature ends—that is, attack and calcine those otherwise insurmountable gates of the solar fortress, namely **gold**. In this way, one fire ignites another—specifically, one sulfur ignites the other. While this occurs, the element of fire dominates, which is the second principle in the solar body; for the fire that resides in gold is called <term>sulfur</term> and <term>soul</term>. 

Where the fire now triumphs, the watery element—namely the moist, fugitive **mercury**—must fly toward its star. Since the mercurial spirit is the dwelling place of the soul and is called the "bond" <note>original: "vinculum"</note> that joins the body with the soul, the first separation follows, along with the dissolution of soul and body. For this purpose, however, that other **cold metallic fire** must also be employed, which is [drawn] from a certain mineral, not yet melted, of Sa-

...must be extracted from **Saturn**, and which is also called the **Mercury of Saturn**. 20. When gold is amalgamated with the Mercury of Saturn, the gold becomes porous. Then, the **infernal fire** <note>A term for a powerful chemical heat or a specific corrosive agent used to break down substances</note> can <term>calcine</term> <note>To reduce a substance to a powder through heat</note> that solid body much faster and more effectively, igniting the solar fire from all sides and reducing it to ashes. From this, we extract the sulfur using "clear heavenly dew," and from the remaining body, after proper <term>reverberation</term> <note>Heating a substance in a furnace where the flames are reflected or "reverberated" onto the material</note>, we leach out that most precious medicinal **Salt**, of which the Sages said: *The Salt of metals is the Philosophers’ Stone* <note>original: "Sal metallorum Lapis est Philosophorum"</note>. Then another philosopher says: *If God had not created salt, the Philosophers' Stone could not be made* <note>original: "Ni Deus creâsset salem, Lapis philosophorum fieri non posset"</note>. This salt, as is proper, must be clarified with <term>spirit of wine</term> <note>original: "spiritu vini"; high-proof alcohol or ethanol</note>. Once this is done, it is united with its sulfur and "imbibed" with the <term>spirit of the world</term> <note>original: "spiritu mundi"; a vital essence believed by alchemists to permeate the universe</note>—that is, with the spirit distilled from the Mercury of Saturn. It is then putrefied and fixed within a single glass vessel and furnace. Thus the **Great Work** <note>original: "magnum Opus"</note> is perfected, leading to fermentation and increase; it is a **universal medicine** for all illnesses. Whoever uses it achieves a renewal of their spirit and a strengthening of all their failing powers. For those who wish to know how and when to apply this medicine, I will—lest I be delayed too long—refer them to the books of the philosophers and continue with my intended purpose.

21. # PLAIN RECAPITULATION.

...more clearly than any philosopher has ever written, I have brought into the open; yet there is still a tiny detail that I have kept hidden from you, namely: how from a certain non-molten, unmalleable mineral **Saturn** <note>original: "Saturno"; the alchemical name for lead</note> such a sublime, rare, and noble **Mercury** <note>original: "Mercurius"</note> is to be extracted, and how it is furthermore to be driven into a red spirit. This can be done through only one single way and medium, about which I have indeed shed light above; but I hope that he whom God does not favor in this matter will neither grasp it nor be able to perceive it.

22. Secondly, I have not only reserved for myself part of the adaptation of the cold metallic fire, but also the preparation of the fiery *Magical* key. As you have heard many times, this key is prepared from two contrary and clashing fires—namely, from sulfur and nitre. Although both of these may be called "infernal fires" <note>Chemical agents that are highly reactive or corrosive</note> that oppose each other, they must nonetheless become one for this specific purpose and produce a single effect. As to how this union is achieved, you must pray to God for the illumination of your mind; I have clearly performed my duty and have revealed more than enough in this little book. My reason is the love of my neighbor <note>original: "charitas proximi"</note>, whom I would gladly wish to encourage with my meager experience and lead back to the right path. For what does my wisdom profit me? What is a talent buried in the earth? Truly, nothing. Out of consideration for this, I have been moved to such a clear proclamation of the truth, especially after I had considered this saying:

> Your knowledge is nothing, unless another knows that you know it. <note>original: "Scire tuum nihil est, nisi, te scire hoc, sciat alter." — a quote from the Roman satirist Persius</note>

Secondly, it is also worthy and just that everything which is good should be shared in common—specifically among those who have bound and devoted themselves to the philosophers and are numbered among them. But for others who are on the outside, all things are done through parables <note>original: "similitudinem"; meaning metaphors or allegories</note>, so that in hearing they may not understand, and in seeing they may not grasp. We shall scatter no pearls before swine, for they would only trample them and value them as nothing, etc.

### COMMENTARY ON THE PHILOSOPHERS' STONE

...I shall not pass over the consideration of both that **Saturn** <note>original: "Saturni"; Lead</note> and **Mercury** <note>original: "Mercurii"</note> here; therefore, lend your ears solely to my teaching. You have heard above that from the **Moon** <note>original: "Luna"; Silver</note>, and similarly from that cold **Saturn of Aries** <note>original: "Arietino Saturno"; likely a reference to Antimony or a specific preparation of lead associated with the zodiac sign of Aries</note>, a certain **Mercury** can be made, and that this serves specifically for the **Work of the Wise** <note>The creation of the Philosophers' Stone</note>. *Secondly*, that from the mineral of **Venus** <note>original: "Veneris"; Copper</note> it is also possible to produce a certain **Solar Mercury** <note>Mercury refined to a gold-like state</note> which is endowed with **solar sulfur** <note>The active, fiery principle of gold</note>, whence I also baptized it in that place as the "Mercury of the Sun," since it is to be used for the generation of **Gold** <note>original: "Solis"</note>. *Thirdly*, that I, notwithstanding this, have already used the Mercury of Saturn for the destruction of gold; thus, regarding this doubt, I say that even the **red Mercury** can be used in the **white Lunar tincture** with great and better advantage. And just as we are not able to move from one extreme to another without a medium, in no other way can we arrive at any **red tincture** unless the **white** is held first. Thus the *kind reader* may now resolve his own scruple and recall that I have written here not of the **Most General Universal**, but only of the **Simple Universal**.

24. The **Most General Universal** <note>original: "Univerſale Generaliſſimum"; the ultimate, all-purpose medicine or transmuting agent</note> is produced from a **double Mercury**, as I have related above, and it is animated and fermented with **solar sulfur**, and fixed with the enduring **salt of gold**; furthermore, it is augmented infinitely through two other sulfurs, both in quantity and quality. The quality, like life itself, is fed by the sulfur; the quantity is increased by the aforementioned Mercury, which carries with it not only the character and power of the **Venereal property** <note>Copper-like qualities, often associated with heat</note>, but also the nature of the cold mineral **Saturn**. For this reason, it is likened to a **double Mercury** and is called **duplicated Mercury**, to which all qualities are assigned; for it has the quality of **Venus** by reason of its hot sulfur, and coldness on the part of **Saturn**. Let the *pure and rivaling Lover of the art* cast aside every doubt, I pray, and place faith in the truth of my experience. You may do whatever you wish, so long as you cannot accuse me of any lie, because I have not begged for this from other books to procure for myself a famous name in some way; rather, through the labor of my hands, I have tested...

Through this First Matter, any metal can be reduced into its three principles <note>Salt, Sulfur, and Mercury</note>, and the true **Potable Gold** <note>original: "aurum Potabile"; a legendary medicinal liquid made from gold, believed to grant health and longevity</note> ought to be made. This First Matter has been sketched out for you in express words, just as both elements—or the **fiery key** <note>original: "ignea clavis"; the essential catalyst or heat required to unlock the secrets of the matter</note>—were demonstrated so clearly, indeed so transparently, to your very eyes that I believe you could not desire anything clearer.

# MEMORIAL

# READER.

<margin>1.</margin> Kind reader, since in my preceding writings I have made one or another obligation which might turn to the benefit and use of the gracious Reader, and furthermore, since I have promised to allow the true, irreducible **Potable Gold** <term>Aurum Potabile: A legendary liquid preparation of gold believed to be a universal cure and a means of longevity</term> to be prepared and perfected, so that those who require this as a **Universal Medicine** <term>Universali Medicina: A "cure-all" for all physical and spiritual ailments, often identified with the Philosopher's Stone</term> might be able to seek and obtain it: And since I also, for singular and weighty reasons, am intended to fix my residence in a certain place; meanwhile, however, so that I may keep my obligation and promises made by my word inviolate, I ought by right to inform the sincere Reader where I am to be sought; because in the lack of such information, the obligation and promises grow faint and bear the appearance of mere boasting. # MEMORIAL TO THE READER.

*...or rather the **soul of the Sun** <note>original: "anima Solis"; in alchemy, this refers to the "sulfur" or essential essence of gold</note> is at hand, it must be dissolved amicably into an oil without noise or burning by means of that familiar Philosophical Spirit, etc. Hence, with the mediation of the spirit of wine, **Potable Gold** <term>Aurum Potabile: A legendary liquid preparation of gold believed to be a universal medicine</term> is produced; otherwise, and even without it, the tincture is made through **Vulcan** <note>original: "Vulcanum"; the alchemical personification of fire or the furnace</note>. In that case, however, the **Salt of gold** <note>original: "Sal auri"</note> must be present, which can easily be obtained from a certain dead body from which the soul has departed <note>An allegorical way of describing the metallic residue left after the "soul" or essence has been extracted</note>; thus, besides the three usual principles, a fourth something may still be seen, which I baptize as the **earthly curse** <note>original: "terrestre maledictum"</note> and the **sinning matter**, or the receptacle of its own evil and another's good.*

*Wherever now, by the help of this kind of separation, the tincture is extracted from the solar sulfur by the **Universal Solvent** <term>Universale Menstruum: A powerful solvent, often called the Alkahest, capable of reducing substances to their primary matter</term>, no reduction to the prior form <note>i.e., back into solid, malleable metal</note> is to be hoped for or achieved for all eternity. This is because the malleable metallic body must derive its hardness and malleability from its own Salt, but here there is only the pure soul and the **spirit of Hermes** <note>original: "spiritus Hermetis"; the volatile essence associated with Mercury/Hermes</note>, etc. Therefore, our solution, or rather our **true and irreducible potable gold**, ought to be so named, which I teach here in the truth of the matter. For that reason, let the honest Reader trust me and doubt not that a certain tincture can be obtained through this.*

<margin>3.</margin> *But restore to that glorified fiery soul its own clarified body and Salt, and through the salt, lead this animated spirit back into coagulation; thus the spiritual is made corporal, etc. You indeed shall see what the Most High is going to give you, if you wait for the time with patience and foresight, attributing honor to Him alone. For I am nothing more than a **voice crying in the wilderness** <note>A biblical reference to John the Baptist, positioning the author as a herald of greater truths</note>, which proclaims to you the light for attaining **Wisdom, Wealth, and Health** <note>original: "Sapientiæ, Opulentiæ, Sanitatiſque"</note>; that light is the **Alpha and Omega** <note>The beginning and the end</note>, the bow and the stern of all things.*

# The Correctness of the Work.

->*As much, indeed, as is known until now.*<-

No large or serious errors are present; however, minor ones (namely by the transposition or change of some letter), and indeed very few of them, have crept in. It should therefore be read as follows:

Page 7, line 18: **Maecenas** <note>original: "Mecœnati"; the author is correcting the spelling of the name of the famous Roman patron of the arts to use the 'œ' diphthong</note> with the *œ* diphthong in the middle, instead of *Maecenati*.

P. 12, verse 4: **Messenger** <note>original: "Nuntius"</note>, instead of *Muntius*, with an *M*; a printer's error: and likewise in the same place, **it is said** <note>original: "dicitur"</note>, instead of *diciter*.

P. 27, verse 3: **Westerners** <note>original: "Hesperios"</note>, instead of *Hesperidos* <note>Referring to the Hesperides, the nymphs of the sunset</note>, but only in some copies.

P. 55, second to last line: **lampoons** <note>original: "sillos"; from the Greek "silloi," referring to satirical poems</note>, in place of **witticisms** <note>original: "sales," literally "salts"</note>, for the sake of the verse.

Likewise in the same place, the last line: **Proverb-writer** <note>original: "Parœmiographo"</note>, with the *œ* diphthong, instead of *Paremiographo*, with the *æ* diphthong.

p. 66, l. 11: **hear ye** <note>original: "audite"</note>, instead of **to hear** <note>original: "audire"</note>, because the sense will be better connected this way.

p. 80, v. 2: **now** <note>original: "nunc"</note>, instead of *nnnc*, with three *n*s.

p. 82, v. 11: **flowed down** <note>original: "defluxit"</note>, instead of **melted away** <note>original: "distabuit"</note> (for the sake of the syllable's poetic quantity and for better meaning); and this only in a few copies.

p. 116, l. 25: **world** <note>original: "mundum"</note>, instead of *mundnm*, with one *u*.

p. 125, l. 10: **canopies** <note>original: "conopeis"; referring to mosquito nets or coverings</note>, without the *œ* diphthong, instead of *conopœis*, with the same; also in very few copies.

p. 128, l. 18: **by prudence** <note>original: "prudentiâ"</note>, instead of **prudent**, by the carelessness of the printer, though in very few copies.

p. 157, l. 21: **Sibyls** <note>original: "Sibyllæ"; the legendary prophetesses of antiquity</note>, instead of *Sibullæ*, but in many copies.

p. 216, l. 25: **chain** <note>original: "catenâ"</note>, instead of *cathenâ*, with the aspiration <note>The author is correcting a "medievalism" where an unnecessary 'h' was added to Latin words</note>.

p. 281, v. 2. or l. 8: **Who** <note>original: "Qui"</note>, instead of *Qui7*, with a small mark and the cipher *7*; but only in certain copies; a printer's error.

p. 291, l. 5: **of his journey** <note>original: "itineris sui"</note>, instead of **of their** <note>original: "suis"</note>: nearly the greatest fault that I know to be in here.

p. 63: read **-tato**, instead of **-de**, the final syllable or indicative tail; by the carelessness and error of the printer.

p. finally 67, l. 1: **two Saturns** <note>original: "Saturnos duos"; changing the grammar from nominative to the accusative case</note>, instead of *Saturnus duos*; truly the greatest error that exists, etc.

<meta>This page is the "Menda," or Errata list, continuing from the final pages of the main text. It serves as a quality control measure common in early modern printing, where the author provides a list of corrections for mistakes made by the typesetter during the production process.</meta>

# E R R O R S
## The Correctness of the Work.

->Errors to the reader.<-

I have not found any great errors; however, minor ones (should they not displease anyone) have crept in through neglect or haste, with very few exceptions. You shall correct them as follows:

Page 7, line 18: **Maccataei** <note>original: "Maccataei"; likely referring to the Maccabees or a specific proper name</note> with a diphthong in the middle, instead of *Maccataei*.

P. 12, verse 4: **Weddings** <note>original: "Nuptiis"</note> instead of **Of Weddings** <note>original: "Nuptiar[um]"</note>, by a printer's error. Likewise in the same place, **it is said** <note>original: "dicitur"</note> is used for **it is said**.

P. 29, verse 3: **Hebrews** <note>original: "Hebraeos"</note> instead of *Hepraeos*, though only in some copies.

P. 55, second to last lines: **those** <note>original: "illos"</note> in place of **those**, for the sake of the meter <note>original: "propter carmen"; indicating a correction to the rhythm of a poem</note>.

In the same place, second to last line: **Pre-named** <note>original: "Praenominato"</note> with the *ae* diphthong, instead of **Of the pre-named** <note>original: "Praenominatorum"</note> with the diphthong.

P. 66, line 11: **to hear** <note>original: "audire"</note> instead of **to hear**, because the connection of the sentence will be better this way.

P. 80, verse: **for** <note>original: "nam"</note> instead of *nam*, which was an error for *p. n.* <note>The translator notes this likely refers to a specific typesetting slip where the letters 'p' and 'n' were substituted or added</note>.

P. 85, verse 11: **he had said** <note>original: "dixerat"</note> instead of **he said** <note>original: "dixit"</note> (on account of the quantity of the syllable, and better for both), expressed in certain editions.

P. 116, line 25: **world** <note>original: "mundum"</note> instead of **pure** <note>original: "mundam"</note>, with a single *u*.

P. 125, line 10: **visible things** <note>original: "conspicua"</note> are with the *ae* diphthong, instead of *conspicua* with the same; likewise in those same copies.

P. 128, line 18: **prudence** <note>original: "prudentia"</note> instead of **to the prudent one** <note>original: "prudenti"</note>, as the printer found, although in very few copies.

P. 157, line 12: **Sibyl** <note>original: "Sibylla"</note> instead of **Of the Sibyl** <note>original: "Sibyllae"</note>, and in several copies.

P. 215, line 25: **circus** <note>original: "circus"</note> instead of **circus**, using a diphthong.

P. 281, verse 3, line 8: **Who** <note>original: "Qui"</note> instead of **Who**, with the mark and the letter **alpha** <note>original: "& alpha;"; likely a Greek letter 'α' used as a reference mark or a typo</note>; but this error of the printer is heard only in certain copies.

P. 291, line 5: **for the traveler** <note>original: "itineranti"</note> instead of **to travel** <note>original: "itinerari" </note>: namely, the greatest thing that is said.

P. 563: Read **rarely** <note>original: "raro"</note> for the last syllable or the same indicative as found by the error of the printer.

Finally, p. 61, line 1: **The two highest** <note>original: "Summos duos"</note> instead of **The two Lords** <note>original: "Summos dnos," where 'dnos' is a common abbreviation for 'dominos'</note> (this is an error regarding the greatest shrines, as is understood).

<term>Orations</term> (Orationes): formal speeches or addresses, often religious or philosophical in nature.
<term>Commentary</term> (Expositio): a detailed explanation or interpretation of a text.
<term>Encouragement</term> (Incentivum): a motivating text or "incentive" toward a specific virtue.
<term>Hymns</term> (Hymni): sacred songs or poems.
<term>Statutes</term> (Statutorum): the formal rules or laws of an organization or discipline.
<term>Triumphant matters</term> (Triumphalia): writings celebrating a victory, here likely a spiritual one.
<term>Kindness/Indulgence</term> (Indulgentia): though often associated with the Catholic Church's remission of punishment, here it likely refers to charitable relief or mercy.
<term>Arguments</term> (Argumenta): summaries or logical outlines of the content to follow.
<term>Magic Language</term> (Lingua Magica): the study of occult or sacred languages believed to hold inherent power.
<term>Instructions</term> (Institutiones): foundational teachings or principles of a specific field of study.
<term>Testimonies</term> (Testimonia): evidence or supporting statements from other authors or members of a brotherhood.
<term>Judgments</term> (Iudiciorum): formal decisions or critiques regarding conduct and study.
<term>Image</term> (Imago): a symbolic representation or portrait of an ideal figure.
<term>Song of Styles</term> (Cantu Stylorum): a metaphorical term for the aesthetic or spiritual rhythm of writing.
